_comment: Site editorial, NOT paper text. One plain-language sentence per technique, written for readers meeting a term for the first time. Rendered under an explicit 'In brief — site editorial, not from the paper' label. Flagged for author review before publication.

summaries.training: The original build of a model — learning its parameters from scratch on a large dataset — included here as a reference point rather than as a post-training technique.
summaries.fullft: Continues training every weight in the model on new task data — maximum flexibility, maximum cost, and no part of the model left unchanged.
summaries.partft: Retrains only the later layers and freezes the early ones, so the general features learned during pre-training stay intact and less needs re-testing.
summaries.peft: Freezes the base model and trains a small add-on instead, so the original weights are never touched and the adapter can be swapped out or removed cleanly.
summaries.reft: Trains small permanent modules that adjust the model's internal activations as it runs, leaving the base weights themselves unchanged.
summaries.da: Trains a model to close the gap when the data seen at deployment looks different from the training data, without needing many labels for the new domain.
summaries.fsl: Learns a new task from a handful of labelled examples by actually updating weights — as opposed to just showing examples in the prompt, which is ICL.
summaries.retraining: Trains the existing model again on newer data to recover accuracy lost as the world drifted away from the original training distribution.
summaries.cl: Learns a sequence of tasks over time while trying not to forget earlier ones — the central difficulty being catastrophic forgetting.
summaries.til: Continual learning where you know which task an input belongs to, so the model can route to task-specific parameters.
summaries.dil: Continual learning where the task stays the same but the input distribution keeps shifting, so the model must track a moving target.
summaries.sft: Trains a model on curated instruction-and-response pairs so it answers in the format and manner people expect.
summaries.rlhf: Uses human preference comparisons to train a reward model, then tunes the model against it — the standard route to making outputs helpful and safe.
summaries.dpo: Reaches the same goal as RLHF directly from preference pairs, skipping the separate reward model and the reinforcement-learning loop.
summaries.rlaif: Replaces human preference labels with AI-generated ones, guided by a written set of principles rather than case-by-case human judgement.
summaries.rlvr: Trains on tasks where answers can be checked automatically — maths, code, proofs — so the reward signal comes from a verifier rather than an opinion.
summaries.lp: Trains a small classifier on the model's internal representations to see what information they contain, without changing the model itself.
summaries.leace: Surgically removes a concept's linear influence from the model's representations — used for fairness work — with a closed-form edit rather than training.
summaries.advrstrn: Trains on deliberately perturbed inputs so the model holds up against adversarial examples rather than breaking on small, crafted changes.
summaries.metalrn: Trains a model to be good at learning new tasks quickly, rather than good at any one task — "learning to learn".
summaries.mtl: Trains one model on several related tasks at once so they share representations and reinforce each other.
summaries.selfplay: Improves a model by having it compete against or critique itself, generating its own training signal without external labels.
summaries.currilrn: Orders training examples from easy to hard, so the model builds up competence in stages rather than facing everything at once.
summaries.activelrn: Lets the model choose which examples get labelled next, concentrating scarce annotation effort where it will help most.
summaries.dataaug: Expands the training set with transformed copies of existing data, improving robustness without collecting anything new.
summaries.semisl: Trains on a small labelled set alongside a large unlabelled one, drawing a learning signal from the unlabelled data rather than leaving it unused.
summaries.ssl: Continues pre-training on unlabelled data from a specialist domain, so the model absorbs its patterns and vocabulary before any task-specific tuning.
summaries.dpft: Fine-tunes with mathematical privacy guarantees, bounding how much any single training record can influence the resulting model.
summaries.fl: Trains across many devices or institutions without centralising their data — each site computes updates locally and only those are shared.
summaries.kd: Trains a smaller model to imitate a larger one's outputs, keeping much of the capability at a fraction of the serving cost.
summaries.compress: Shrinks a model through quantisation, pruning, or similar, so it fits and runs where the original could not.
summaries.taskarith: Combines separately tuned models by arithmetic on their weights — adding capabilities, or subtracting them by negating a task vector.
summaries.lce: Extends how much text a model can attend to at once, so longer documents fit in a single pass.
summaries.moe: Adapts a model by adding expert sub-networks or training the router that picks between them, so capacity grows without every parameter running on every input.
summaries.pe: Changes what you write in the prompt to steer the model — no weights change, and by default the effect lasts only for that request.
summaries.pl: Learns the prompt itself as trainable parameters rather than writing it by hand — continuous vectors prepended to the input.
summaries.apo: Automatically searches for better prompt wording, optimising the instruction rather than the model.
summaries.rag: Retrieves relevant documents at query time and puts them in the context, so the model can use knowledge it was never trained on.
summaries.icl: Shows the model a few worked examples in the prompt, adapting it for that request only, with no training and no artifact left behind.
summaries.ce: Manages everything that goes into the model's context — retrieved documents, tools, history — as a maintained, versioned production asset.
summaries.tta: Temporarily updates the model's weights at inference using the test input itself, usually to absorb a distribution shift, then reverts them before the next prediction.
summaries.ttcompute: Spends more computation at answer time — sampling more, searching further, reasoning longer — without changing a single weight.
summaries.calib: Adjusts the model's confidence so its stated probabilities match how often it is actually right, leaving its accuracy unchanged.
summaries.crossmodel: Trains image and text representations into a shared space so the model can relate what it sees to what it reads.
summaries.modeladapter: Inserts a small trainable module into one modality's own pathway inside a multimodal model, improving that input type without retraining the shared backbone.
summaries.multimodinstr: Instruction-tunes on paired image-and-text examples so a multimodal model follows directions about what it is shown.
summaries.munlrn: Removes specific data or knowledge from a trained model, often to meet privacy obligations, aiming to leave it behaving as though it had never seen the material.
summaries.ke: Edits an individual fact inside a model, changing one specific association while aiming to leave unrelated knowledge undisturbed.
summaries.actsteer: Nudges the model's internal activations at run time to push behaviour in a chosen direction, without changing any weights and lasting only for that run.
